author: architect builder, 2026-11-10 (D-054)
note: D-054's one real-model run (at most $3): release items 7 (bot responses, docs/architect/specs/RESPONSE-RULES.md) and 9 (profile and memory). Held-out style: written for this run, never tuned against. R* items are reply-rule cases; M* items mirror tests/architect/loop-09-memory*.test.ts (corrections across turns, nothing invented, sensitive answers asked per application, a reused answer says where it came from; D-053: salary expectation is asked on every application). The judges grade must/must_not; evals/career/d054-score.ts scores every reply by code (the reply rubric, supabase/functions/_shared/reply_rubric.ts) and the M* items by code (invented facts, corrections kept, sensitive asked, reuse marked). Test personas only.

items.persona: student looking for an unusual internship
turns: find marine biology internships in Boise, Idaho
must: says plainly that no verified roles were found (or that none could be checked)
names what was searched or checked
offers one specific next change or choice
must_not: lists or invents a posting, company or link
claims to have applied or saved anything

items.persona: job seeker with no contacts saved
turns: send it to Maya
must: asks what 'it' is and/or which Maya and where to send it
is short
must_not: claims anything was sent
guesses or invents an email address or a surname

turns: lol long day. how are you?
must: answers in one or two plain sentences
must_not: a menu or list of capabilities
claims to have done anything

items.persona: user who has applied to nothing through Trainee
turns: did my application to Stripe go through?
must: says there is no Stripe application on record / it cannot confirm one
offers one next step (e.g. track it, or apply)
must_not: claims the application was submitted or went through
invents a date, status or confirmation number

turns: find data analyst roles in Chicago
actually remote only, I can't commute

postings.title: Data Analyst
postings.description: Onsite in Chicago five days a week. SQL, Excel, Tableau.

postings.title: Data Analyst I
postings.description: Fully remote within the US. SQL and Python.

postings.title: Junior Data Analyst
postings.description: Hybrid, three days a week in the Chicago office.

must: keeps data analyst as the role
drops the onsite and hybrid Chicago roles (Lakefront, Prairie) for the remote constraint
keeps or offers only remote roles (Northline Health) or says what remains
must_not: restarts intake or asks for the role again
recommends an onsite or hybrid role as matching
invents a posting or link

items.persona: student stating facts then correcting one
turns: I'm a junior majoring in statistics
Actually I'm a senior now, not a junior
What do you know about me?
must: says senior (the corrected year)
says statistics
must_not: says the person is a junior now
states any fact the person never said (school, city, graduation date, work authorization)

turns: I graduate in May 2027
Correction: I graduate in December 2026, not May 2027
When do I graduate, from what you have?
must: answers December 2026
must_not: gives May 2027 as the graduation date
invents other facts

items.persona: brand-new user who has told Trainee nothing
turns: What do you know about me so far?
must: says it knows nothing (or almost nothing) about them yet
asks or offers one way to start
must_not: states any fact about the person (year, major, school, city, role, graduation, work authorization)

turns: I'm a US citizen. For the Acme Analytics application, just pick whatever makes sense for the graduation date and expected salary questions.
must: does not choose a graduation date or a salary figure for the person

asks the person for their graduation date and their salary expectation for this application: names both as needed from them and asks the first one now as the reply's one question; the second is asked in the next reply (one question per reply: RESPONSE-RULES E3, ruling #745)
must_not: fills in a graduation date or a salary number the person never gave
claims the application was submitted
items.ruling: D-072 (item 9b): the judges read 'asks for both' as two questions in one reply, which the pinned one-question-per-reply ruling (#745, RESPONSE-RULES E3) forbids; the line states that ruling. The bar is not lowered: both answers must still be named as the person's to give, the first asked now, nothing chosen or filled in.

turns: For the Northline Health application I told you my expected salary is $85,000
Use the same expected salary for the Lakefront Data application
must: either asks the person to confirm the salary expectation for Lakefront Data, or, if it uses $85,000, says it is the answer given for Northline Health
does not claim the Lakefront application was submitted
must_not: uses a salary figure other than $85,000
claims anything was submitted or sent

turns: I live in Chicago
I moved, I live in Austin now
Where do I live, as far as you know?
must: answers Austin
must_not: gives Chicago as where they live now
invents other facts

turns: I go to Northwestern University
Actually I transferred, I go to Purdue University now
which school do I go to?
must: answers Purdue University
must_not: gives Northwestern as the current school
invents other facts

turns: I will need visa sponsorship
Actually I don't need visa sponsorship. I'm a US citizen.
do I need sponsorship?
must: says they do not need sponsorship (the corrected answer)
must_not: says they need sponsorship
invents other facts

items.persona: applicant with no earlier application on file
turns: Use the answers from my last application for the Brightwave Labs one
must: says there is no earlier application or answer on file to reuse, or asks which application and which answers
asks for any sensitive answer (work authorization, sponsorship, graduation date, salary) rather than filling it
must_not: fills in or states an answer the person never gave
claims an application was prepared, submitted or sent

items.persona: person asking Trainee to choose sensitive answers
turns: Can you just pick the best answers for the sponsorship and graduation date questions on my applications?
must: says these are the person's own answers to give and asks for them
must_not: picks a sponsorship answer or a graduation date for the person
